meta.purpose: The raw data layer — external-source data held exactly as the source gave it: verse text, verse morphology, and the Strong's lexicon. This process owns WHAT RAW IS and the controls that let it be trusted; it owns no interpretation whatsoever.
meta.the_one_rule: RAW IS IMMUTABLE. Write-once from the source, never overwritten by later processing. Every downstream layer references it and none may mutate it. This is the layer the whole study rests on: if raw drifts, every finding above it is unfalsifiable — and the programme has already lost a database once (2026-06-03).
meta.envelope: Every item carries the common rule envelope — see ../_manifest.json meta.envelope. Its vocabularies (governs · kind · status · validation.axis · validation.enforcement · validation.severity) are defined there and are NOT restated here.
meta.why_this_file_is_the_simple_case: Raw has no [I] rules at all. Every control is deterministic and most are expressible in DB technology — so this file is the clearest demonstration of the 2026-07-15 enforcement ruling: the rules live HERE, and `validation.enforcement` says which of them the schema projects as a CHECK / FK / NOT NULL / index.

nodes.process: How the layer works — immutability, provenance stamping, what qualifies as raw, and the boundary against `fetch` (which retrieves) and `base` (which derives).
nodes.entities: The data it owns: verse · verse_morphology · lexicon. Definitional only — what each entity IS and how they relate. It does NOT declare tables or columns; that is the schema's job (layout v2 §1).
nodes.output: What the layer emits for human consumption. Raw emits almost nothing — it is consumed, not published.
nodes.validation: The ingest controls. Source-parity, completeness, no-null, FK integrity. Mostly db:*-enforced.

open.issue: `gate.raw.source-parity` is stated but has no mechanism: STEP is a live local server with NO cache, so re-querying it later is not a stable baseline to compare against — the source can change under us and we would not know.
open.consequence: The most important raw control — 'is this what the source actually said' — is currently unenforceable. Migrating the live DB's raw layer as-is (plan 3.4.1) inherits this: it is trusted, not verified.
options: A: snapshot the STEP response verbatim at ingest (a raw_source_payload store) and parity-check against the snapshot, not the server
B: checksum per verse/term at ingest; re-fetch and compare on demand
C: accept trust-on-first-ingest; parity is a spot-check only
open.recommendation: A — it makes raw genuinely replayable and is the only option that survives STEP changing or going away. It is also what 'raw is immutable' actually requires: you cannot assert immutability against a source you did not keep.

open.issue: The plan migrates the live DB's raw layer as-is, stamped `migrated-from-<old>@<date>` (3.4.1). But that data's TRUE provenance is a STEP fetch of unknown date, made under the old engine.
open.consequence: `prov.raw.source-stamp` would record the migration, not the origin — provenance that documents the copy rather than the source.
open.recommendation: Stamp both: `source` = STEP (+ fetch date where recoverable, else `unknown`), `migrated_from` = the old DB. Never let the migration stamp masquerade as the origin.
open.resolve_by: researcher decision; affects the migration module

process.reference: plan §3.4 'The DB holds results in four distinct layers'
process.intent: Define what qualifies as raw, so the boundary against derived data is not a judgement call at write time.
process.satisfaction: A row is raw if and only if its every field came from an external source verbatim, with no conversion, derivation, inference or methodological processing applied.

spec.statement: Raw = untouched external-source data. Anything converted, parsed, derived or judged is BASE, not raw — even if it is mechanical.

boundary_examples.raw: the morph_code string as STEP returned it
boundary_examples.base: the `stem` derived FROM that morph_code — derivation makes it base, however deterministic

spec.note: This boundary is what makes `raw.immutable` enforceable. A layer that quietly admits derived values cannot be immutable, because derivations change when their rules change.

process.intent: Guarantee that the evidentiary floor never moves, so any finding can be re-derived from the same raw and any drift is attributable to the layer above.
process.satisfaction: No UPDATE or DELETE has ever touched a raw row. Corrections arrive as a new versioned ingest, never as an edit.

spec.statement: Raw tables are write-once. Downstream layers reference them and never mutate them. A correction is a new ingest with its own provenance, not an edit of the old row.
spec.enforcement_note: db: revoke UPDATE/DELETE at the schema level where SQLite permits (triggers). gate: the validation engine refuses any patch whose target is a raw table and whose op is not INSERT.
spec.rationale: The 2026-06-03 DB loss was survivable only where work was replayable. An immutable raw layer is what makes replay possible at all.

process.authority: plan §3.4.2 'Don't: no analytical values on mechanical tables'; failure record 02-failures §eisegesis
process.intent: Prevent the specific failure where interpretation was stamped onto mechanical tables (role / char_candidate / characteristic written onto verse_span_index), which destroyed layer separation and made the analysis un-auditable.
process.satisfaction: No raw entity carries a field whose value is a reading, judgement, classification or characteristic.

spec.statement: An interpretive value must never be written onto a raw entity. Layers stay separated.
spec.history: The live DB's `verse_span_index` carries role/char_candidate/characteristic/ib_char_id — which is why the migration strips them and keeps only the structural span (plan 3.4.1).

process.intent: Separate retrieval from storage, so a fetch failure and a raw defect are distinguishable.
process.satisfaction: `fetch` owns talking to STEP (pagination, the 60-cap sectioning, retries, Strong's resolution); `raw` owns what is stored and its controls. Neither restates the other.

spec.statement: Fetch retrieves; raw stores and guards. The handoff is the ingest gate.
spec.three_way_boundary: util.step = HOW STEP is reached and what it can do. fetch = WHAT to retrieve and when. raw = WHAT IS STORED and its controls. Three homes, no overlap (layout v2 §2.3).

process.subject: raw-source
process.authority: researcher 2026-07-15 ('raw needs to cross reference to the utility')
process.intent: Bind the raw layer to the utility that sources it, and require every raw row to name WHICH STEP API produced it — because 'it came from STEP' is not a provenance, there is more than one API and they are not interchangeable.
process.satisfaction: Every raw row names its source API (enum.step_api), the version it was fetched under, and resolves to a fetch-log entry.

spec.statement: STEP is the ONLY source of raw. Every raw row records its source API, its version, and its fetch.

api_binding.never: search.masterSearch.text — English-text hits are not original-language occurrences (step.api-set the_text-search_rule)

spec.one_home_note: The STEP access rules live in utility/step.json and are CITED here (layout v2 §2.3). This rule says only what RAW requires of its source; it does not restate how STEP is reached.

entities.authority: live DB schema 3.40.0 (measure layer, proven — plan §4)
entities.intent: The verse as Scripture gives it — the addressable unit the entire study hangs off. Every finding, span and passage resolves to a verse.
entities.satisfaction: One row per canonical verse; text verbatim; addressable by reference.

does_not_hold: passage_id · is_passage_anchor · process_marker · genre — these are BASE (derived by verses-passages), not raw, though the live DB carries them ON the verse row
spec.note: ⚠ In the live 3.40.0 DB, `verse` mixes raw (text) and base (passage_id, genre, process_marker) on one row. The new schema must separate them or the immutability rule cannot hold — a genre re-derivation would be an UPDATE to a raw table. Flagged for Appendix B.
spec.source_utility: util.step — see step.api-set for the API/entity binding; step.connection for the server and version
spec.source_version: the STEP module the row was fetched under (STEP_DEFAULT_VERSION, default ESV_th). PROVENANCE, not preference — see step.version-is-provenance.

entities.intent: The per-word original-language morphology of each verse — the linguistic source of truth. Language, stem and part-of-speech all derive from it, never the reverse.
entities.satisfaction: One row per word-occurrence in a verse, carrying the source's own surface / Strong's / morph_code.

spec.grain: one row per word-occurrence (verse × word position)
does_not_hold: stem · pos — DERIVED from morph_code, therefore BASE (see raw.definition)
spec.authority_rule: morph_code is THE source of truth for language and stem. Anything that contradicts it is wrong, including the registry.
spec.note: ⚠ The live DB carries `stem` and `pos` on this table (plan §4). Under raw.definition those are base. Same separation problem as ent.raw.verse — Appendix B.
spec.source_utility: util.step — see step.api-set for the API/entity binding; step.connection for the server and version
spec.source_version: the STEP module the row was fetched under (STEP_DEFAULT_VERSION, default ESV_th). PROVENANCE, not preference — see step.version-is-provenance.

entities.intent: The Strong's lexicon entry per term — glosses and sub-glosses. Load-bearing far beyond raw: the SUB-GLOSS is the authority for D101 sense, the spine of the whole lexical read.
entities.satisfaction: One row per Strong's number, carrying the source's gloss and sub-glosses verbatim.

spec.identity: Strong's number (zero-padded 4-digit; H/G prefix; suffix letters mark sub-entries)
spec.downstream: lexical.sense-authority binds D101 to this entity's sub-gloss. The 2026-07-14 audit failed D101 precisely because reads recorded interpretation instead of this value (tsaddiq -> 'public good').
spec.note: ⚠ NAME COLLISION: this raw entity `lexicon` is NOT the `lexical` process. See ../_manifest.json meta.open.lexicon-naming.
spec.source_utility: util.step — see step.api-set for the API/entity binding; step.connection for the server and version
spec.source_version: the STEP module the row was fetched under (STEP_DEFAULT_VERSION, default ESV_th). PROVENANCE, not preference — see step.version-is-provenance.

output.authority: plan §3.4.1 'A reconciliation report closes the migration'
output.intent: The human-facing evidence that the raw layer is sound before any study run begins — raw-layer parity, registry completeness, old-vs-new diffs.
output.satisfaction: Report produced, reviewed and signed off by the researcher before the first study run.

spec.note: Raw publishes almost nothing else — it is consumed by every layer above, not read by humans.

validation.intent: Prove that what is stored is what the source actually said — the control that makes every downstream claim falsifiable.
validation.satisfaction: Every raw row matches its source verbatim.

spec.note: ⚠ RECONCILE — no mechanism. STEP is a live server with NO CACHE (step.no-cache-so-cache-to-db), so there is no stable baseline to compare against. This is a STEP CAPABILITY question and is owned by utility/step.json open.step.parity-baseline (recommendation: snapshot the response verbatim at ingest). One decision, one home.

validation.intent: Catch a partial ingest — the failure mode STEP's 60-result cap makes likely, and which silently understates the corpus.
validation.satisfaction: Row counts match the expected count for the scope; no gaps in verse sequence within a chapter.

spec.rationale: STEP caps at 60 results and the client sections around it; a silently truncated section reads as a complete book. 'Coverage was a mirage' is a named prior failure (plan §1.2).
spec.delegation: The 60-cap arithmetic is proved at the SOURCE by gate.step.cap-exhausted (rows == STEP's reported total, every depth). This gate checks the STORED result: expected row counts per book and no verse-sequence gaps. Two gates, two scopes — the source proves the fetch, this proves the store.

validation.intent: Refuse a raw row with a missing required field, rather than discovering it three layers up.
validation.satisfaction: Every required field on every raw entity is non-null.

spec.enforcement_note: PROJECTED AS NOT NULL CONSTRAINTS by the config-maintenance utility. The rule lives here; the schema carries it. Per the 2026-07-15 ruling, the constraint is a projection — never a second definition.

validation.intent: Guarantee morphology and lexicon rows resolve to a real verse and a real Strong's — no orphans, which the live DB has repeatedly produced.
validation.satisfaction: Every FK resolves; no orphan rows in any raw entity.

spec.enforcement_note: PROJECTED AS FOREIGN KEYS by the config-maintenance utility.
spec.history: The live DB required an XREF-duplication clean-up and an orphan clear (schema 3.33.0) because this was convention, not constraint. Plan §3.4.2: enforced by schema + gates, never by convention.

validation.intent: Keep Strong's comparable across every join in the system.
validation.satisfaction: Every Strong's is H|G + zero-padded 4-digit, with optional suffix letter for sub-entries.

spec.rationale: Unpadded Strong's silently fail to join — a live-DB defect class that required zfill-before-compare as a workaround. The constraint removes the workaround.

validation.intent: Enforce raw.immutable at the point of write, since a violation is undetectable after the fact.
validation.satisfaction: No UPDATE or DELETE reaches a raw table.

spec.enforcement_note: db: BEFORE UPDATE / BEFORE DELETE triggers that RAISE. gate: the patch validator rejects any non-INSERT op targeting a raw entity. Defence in depth — this rule is the floor of the whole study.

naming.intent: This process's naming parameters only — the rules themselves live in the wide pattern file and are cited, never restated.

spec.note: Per layout v2 §2.3 this node carries PARAMETERS, not rules. `id frozen at mint`, `zero-pad`, `same-name -> version bump` are wide rules, cited by id and defined nowhere else.

filing.intent: Where this process's human-facing artefacts are filed.
filing.satisfaction: Raw outputs land in the declared tree; superseded versions archived, never overwritten.

spec.note: Parameters only — the archiving and versioning RULES live in the filing utility's config and are cited by id.
